solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Killer taking men from island (4)

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters, here the letters MEN

explanation.surface: A murderer clearing the menfolk off an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island's Spanish spelling, MENORCA (also Minorca), begins with exactly the letters the clue removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer whale is the orca's everyday name, so 'killer' alone is a fair shortening.

clue.text: Snake — concealed one in old rubbish (8)

indicators.note: HID and I go inside O + PAN

blocks.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to rubbish; PAN splits as P...AN

explanation.surface: A snake has hidden something in a heap of old junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' is a verb here, as in 'critics rubbished the film', so it gives PAN rather than junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the zoologist's term for the serpent family, from Greek ophis; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Irresponsible not running a motor limiting energy (8)

indicators.note: CARLESS sets the limits around E

blocks.note: without a car; splits as CAR...LESS

explanation.surface: A verdict that someone who doesn't drive a car is being irresponsible about energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not running a motor' sounds like a breakdown; it just means owning no car.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless and irresponsible both describe someone who takes no proper care.

clue.text: Far from just tie, reportedly jumper too (3,7)

indicators.note: as it is reported, i.e. spoken: we hear KNOT

blocks.note: a knot is a tie; it is said like NOT
a cricket is a jumping insect; a cricket jumper is also a cricketer's sweater

explanation.surface: A fashion complaint: the tie is unfair, and so is the jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair play, from the gentlemanly bat-and-ball game. 'Too' nods to the cricket jumper, a knitted sweater worn by players, so the jumper fits the tie's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something 'not cricket' is unsporting, far from just.

clue.text: No Scottish company put up the drink (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up writes it bottom to top

explanation.surface: A Scottish firm declining to stock a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, as in 'fell in the drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The drink' is British slang for the sea, as in 'fell in the drink', and any great sea will do.

clue.text: Web app destroyed en bloc in computer-aided testing (9)

indicators.note: EN BLOC is wrecked into a new order
the rearranged letters sit inside CAT

blocks.note: CAT is the abbreviation; it splits as CA...T

explanation.surface: A web application wrecked wholesale during computer testing.
explanation.walkthrough: A cancelbot is a program that deletes posts from Usenet newsgroups, so it is a web app of an old-fashioned kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cancelbot is an automated program on the internet, loosely a web application.

clue.text: Former S American people losing area share imprisonment (13)

indicators.note: RACE loses the A that stands for area

blocks.note: the Inca, rulers of Peru before the Spanish

explanation.surface: A former South American people losing land and sharing captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' does double duty: the INCA are a people, and the next 'people' is RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean being locked up, the long word from Latin carcer, a prison.

clue.text: What retainers do: go back to be accepted by family (4,2)

definitions.note: the definition describes an action; the answer is that action as a verb phrase

indicators.note: 'back' as in going back: the letters return the way they came, right to left
KIN takes the reversed letters inside

blocks.note: kin = family; it splits as K...IN
go = urinate, informally; reversed it is EEP

explanation.surface: Advice about returning to be welcomed by the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' in the lavatory sense is PEE; the solver expecting 'go back' to mean return gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Retainers retain, i.e. keep things in, whether a dental brace or a fee.

clue.text: Sinew is key in part of joint (6)

indicators.note: 'in' as a place: D is put in, i.e. inside, TENON

blocks.note: the tenon is the tongue of a mortise-and-tenon woodworking joint; it splits as TEN...ON

explanation.surface: An anatomy note that the sinew is crucial to a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's joint is a knee or elbow; the wordplay's joint is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a sinew joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Rue this getting edited — it’s far from smooth (7)

indicators.note: the letters are rewritten into a new order

explanation.surface: Regretting a rough draft once an editor has been at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue this' reads as regret; it is just letters for the editor to rework.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy, the opposite of smooth-skinned.

clue.text: University member, all very skilful and trustworthy (13)

blocks.note: each, as in 'a pound each' = all of them

explanation.surface: A glowing reference for a college fellow: highly skilled and reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's university member is a fellow or don; in the wordplay the member sits in parliament instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unimpeachable is beyond reproach, entirely trustworthy.

clue.text: Elementary particle London college discovered in gas (7)

indicators.note: to be discovered in a place is to be found inside it, so UCL sits within NEON

blocks.note: neon is a gas; it splits as N...EON

explanation.surface: A London college's physicists find a particle in a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: University College London is known everywhere by its initials, UCL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon, a proton or neutron, is a particle of the atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Sporting league led by duke (9)

indicators.note: D comes first, in front of ALLIANCE

explanation.surface: A sports league headed by an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' is not athletics but the old sense of amorous play, so it is a noun like dalliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting, as a noun, is playful flirtation: dalliance.

clue.text: Recall working with current Human Resources for money? (5)

indicators.note: calling back turns the whole string round

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine is on
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Remembering your job, with HR in charge of the pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money, cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is a dated British slang word for money.

clue.text: Stories involving foal, bees and asps? (6,6)

definitions.text: Stories involving foal, bees and asps?

indicators.note: to involve once meant to roll up or entangle, so the letters are twisted together

explanation.surface: A description of stories whose cast is a foal, some bees and snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Aesop's fables are stories about animals, which the fodder supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop's fables are ancient Greek moral tales starring talking animals.

clue.text: Top grade of seabird circling loch kilometres south (4,5)

indicators.note: circling means going round, so FULMAR flies round L
in a down clue, south is below, so KS comes last

blocks.note: the fulmar is a gull-like seabird; it splits as FUL...MAR
K = kilometres, as in a 10K run

explanation.surface: A top-quality seabird wheeling round a Scottish lake, a few kilometres to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South' does two jobs: it gives S and places the KS below the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Full marks, the maximum score on a test, is the top grade a marker can give; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Pen with second cygnet initially seen on river (8)

indicators.note: only the first letter of cygnet
in a down clue, S + C sits on top of the river

blocks.note: first letter of cygnet; 'seen' just says it shows up
the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, northwest England

explanation.surface: A pen, the female swan, with her young one glimpsed on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, so 'pen' with 'cygnet' paints swans; but it is the verb, to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen is to write, and to scribble is to write hastily.

clue.text: What might prompt island girl to be extravagant (8)

explanation.surface: Asking what pushes a girl from an island to splash out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What might prompt' reads as a question; it is simply a noun phrase for the thing that prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, like the prodigal son.

clue.text: Globe recanted with changes for Romeo perhaps (6,6)

indicators.note: RECANTED's letters are changed round

explanation.surface: The Globe, Shakespeare's theatre, rewriting its Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's London theatre, which sends the solver to the play; Romeo here is the role in Prokofiev's ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is a leading part for a ballet dancer in Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Confused hour trapped in urban environment (6)

indicators.note: to be trapped in something is to be held inside it, so HR is caught inside TOWN

blocks.note: a town; it splits as T...OWN

explanation.surface: Someone bewildered after an hour stuck in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition: thrown means baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown, as in 'the question threw me', means confused.

clue.text: Indian dish, cold, very cold (6)

blocks.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a small wok-like pan
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A menu note on a curry served cold, very cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Baltic is British slang for freezing weather, after the chilly sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, 'it's Baltic' means it's very cold.

clue.text: Erica for PM (5)

blocks.note: Erica is the botanical genus of low moorland shrubs
PM = Prime Minister; this one led Britain 1970–74

explanation.surface: Backing a woman called Erica to become prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a first name; it is the Latin name for heath plants, and Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Heath is the common name for Erica plants, and Heath was a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Tut … was so heartlessly given a penalty on quiet motorway (9)

indicators.note: FINED loses its heart, the middle letter N
in an across clue, the penalty is placed after the rest

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Someone tut-tutting at a harsh penalty on a quiet motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Tut is Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh, and 'was so' completes the definition: he was mummified. The surface reads 'tut' as a sound of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Tutankhamun's body was preserved as a mummy, so 'was so' completes the fact about him.

clue.text: Pondered topping what the entertainer did (5)

indicators.note: cutting off the top, which in a down entry is the first letter

blocks.note: an entertainer amused; topping removes the A

explanation.surface: An entertainer's act that tops everything and leaves the crowd thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' reads as excellent; here it is beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Mused and pondered both mean thought deeply.

clue.text: Time of revolution, men circling court, roubles regularly stolen (7)

indicators.note: circling means going round, so OR surrounds CT
every other letter of roubles
stolen goods are taken in, so OBE is also taken inside OR

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers; it splits as O...R

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries surrounding a court and stealing roubles as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The October Revolution of 1917 brought the Bolsheviks to power in Russia, which is why the roubles fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian revolution of 1917 is named after October, its month in the old calendar.

clue.text: Small lady’s grip drops hot buffet (7)

indicators.note: drops as in lets fall: HANDBAG lets go of its H

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothes labels
HANDBAG, a woman's grip or bag, without H for hot

explanation.surface: A petite woman loses hold of her plate at a hot buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' is the verb, to strike, not a spread of food. A grip is an old word for a travelling bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To sandbag someone is to hit or batter them, to buffet them.

clue.text: Strange clue grasped by inventor over sugar compound (10)

indicators.note: CLUE is made strange, rearranged
the rearranged letters are held inside the inventor
the inventor's name is turned over, reversed

blocks.note: Thomas Edison; reversed it is NOSIDE, split N...OSIDE

explanation.surface: An inventor puzzling over a strange clue in a chemistry problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'about'; here it turns the inventor's name backwards before the clue's letters go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleoside is a compound of a sugar joined to a base, a building block of DNA and RNA.

clue.text: Remedy of blood in ER when heart’s failing (4)

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter M, gives out

blocks.note: hemal, 'of blood', in American spelling (British haemal)
HEMAL without its middle letter M

explanation.surface: Blood given in the emergency room when a patient's heart is failing.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, the American emergency room, signals the American spelling HEMAL rather than the British HAEMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to remedy an ill is to cure it.
